geo.label: Hambantota port: a 99-year lease to China Merchants Port Holdings (2017)
geo.text: Sri Lanka leased a controlling stake in Hambantota International Port to China Merchants Port Holdings on a 99-year lease in 2017, after it could not repay Chinese loans. The port was handed over in December 2017. The lease is widely cited in the debate over Chinese lending.
geo.source: CSIS (Game of Loans); Wikipedia (Hambantota International Port)

geo.label: Chinese defence attaché call on the Army Commander (16 July 2026)
geo.text: The Chinese Defence Attaché and the Chinese Naval Attaché paid a courtesy call on the Army Commander at Army Headquarters on 16 July 2026. This is routine defence diplomacy and describes no deployment.

geo.label: Lakvijaya coal station: a Chinese contractor repaired it after a 2014 outage
geo.text: The Lakvijaya coal power station at Puttalam was commissioned in 2014 at about US$1.35bn. After a 2014 cooling-system outage, a Chinese contractor (CMEC) repaired it. The Ceylon Electricity Board was dissolved on 9 March 2026 under the Sri Lanka Electricity Act.

naval.label: Hambantota: no military base for any country, the government said in 2017
naval.text: The Ports Minister said in 2017 that Hambantota would be a purely commercial port, and that routine port calls by foreign navies would be regulated by Sri Lanka, as in Colombo. The government says the port operates under Sri Lankan law.

naval.label: Two Chinese submarines called at Colombo in 2014 (reported)
naval.text: Two Chinese submarines called at Colombo in 2014, during the last year of the former president's term. Press reports differ on the type of boats, and this build did not verify them.

naval.label: Sri Lanka Navy commands: Eastern at the SLN Dockyard, Trincomalee; Western, Southern and Northern at Colombo, Galle and Karainagar
naval.text: The Navy's headquarters is at Flagstaff Street in Colombo. Its Western Naval Command is at Colombo Harbour, Southern at Galle, Northern at Karainagar in Jaffna and Eastern at the SLN Dockyard in Trincomalee, which is the largest naval base. The Naval and Maritime Academy is at the dockyard.
naval.source: Wikipedia (List of active ships of the Sri Lanka Navy; SLN Dockyard, 2026)

scs.label: Chinese research and tracking ships: Yuan Wang 5 (2022), Shi Yan 6 (2023), and a moratorium from 1 January 2024
scs.text: The tracking ship Yuan Wang 5 berthed at Hambantota for replenishment in August 2022, after Colombo asked for a deferral over security concerns. Shi Yan 6 docked at Colombo for replenishment in October 2023. Sri Lanka imposed a one-year moratorium on foreign research vessels from 1 January 2024 and turned away Xiang Yang Hong 3. In 2026 the government was still finalising a standard operating procedure for foreign research vessels.
scs.source: NBC News (2022); ThePrint (Oct 2023); ORF (Jan 2024); Maritime Executive (Jan 2024); Sunday Times (Mar 2026)

scs.label: Southern sea lanes carry energy and container traffic; Colombo handled 8.29 million TEU in 2025
scs.text: Sea lanes passing south of Sri Lanka carry a large share of energy shipments and container traffic between the Middle East and Asia. The Port of Colombo handled 8.29 million TEUs in 2025, the highest on record. During the 2026 Hormuz crisis, Colombo was among the ports reporting congestion as ships were diverted.

scs.label: Undersea cables: landing points at Colombo, Mount Lavinia and Matara; SEA-ME-WE 5 and 6 land at Matara
scs.text: Sri Lanka has landing stations at Colombo (SEA-ME-WE 4, the Dhiraagu-SLT cable and FALCON), at Mount Lavinia (Sri Lanka Telecom) and at Matara (SEA-ME-WE 5 and 6). Sri Lanka Telecom is the national backbone network provider.

scs.label: Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar: shallow waters on the north coast (general navigation information)
scs.text: The Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar are shallow, which limits the movement of deep-draft ships. This is general navigation information and was not verified in this build.
scs.source: Public information (not verified in this build)

econ.label: Colombo Port City: 269 hectares of reclaimed land; about US$1.4bn invested; a further US$300m committed (January 2026)
econ.text: The Colombo Port City, a special economic zone on 269 hectares of reclaimed land beside Colombo Port, is being built by CHEC, a Chinese company. CHEC has invested about US$1.4bn. It confirmed a further US$300m in January 2026. Full completion is not expected before 2041.
econ.source: Daily Mirror (Jul 2026); Gulf News (May 2025); Global Construction Review (2024)

econ.label: Sinopec refinery at Hambantota: still proposed; delayed over equity, tax, land and market access (June 2026)
econ.text: A Sinopec refinery planned beside Hambantota port has been delayed by disputes over equity, tax concessions, market access and land allocation. The Central Environment Authority has issued terms of reference for an environmental impact study.

econ.label: Trincomalee oil tank farm: 99 tanks; the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation renovates 29 more
econ.text: The Trincomalee oil tank farm at China Bay has 99 tanks, and the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation owns 24. As of August 2026, two had been renovated and tenders had been called for three more. A ready request for proposals covers 29 tanks, with a two-year target. Other tanks are operated under separate arrangements, which this dashboard does not describe.

econ.label: Sapugaskanda refinery: 60 years old; expansion tender pending; a Rs 12.78 bn fuel pipeline tendered
econ.text: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation sought proposals to value its 60-year-old Sapugaskanda refinery before tenders for a long-delayed expansion. Bids closed on 15 June 2026. The corporation has also tendered a fuel pipeline from Colombo Port to Kolonnawa, valued at Rs 12.78 bn.

econ.label: The Foreign Minister calls the Trincomalee tank-farm redevelopment the long-term answer to the 2026 fuel shortage
econ.text: The Foreign Minister described the redevelopment of Trincomalee's oil tank farms as the only credible long-term answer to the energy crisis caused by the conflict in West Asia.

air.label: Mattala Air Force station declared open (2 October 2026)
air.text: The Commander of the Air Force declared the Air Force station at Mattala open on 2 October 2026, under its inaugural commanding officer.

air.label: Air-surveillance and air-defence radar squadrons at China Bay, Hingurakgoda and Vavuniya
air.text: The Air Force operates air-surveillance and air-defence radar squadrons at China Bay (111 Air Surveillance Squadron and No. 6 Air Defence Radar Squadron), at Hingurakgoda (No. 2 Air Defence Radar Squadron) and at Vavuniya. Radar types and suppliers are not described in this dashboard.

air.label: SLAF Katunayake: the largest air base, beside Bandaranaike International Airport; attacked in 2001
air.text: SLAF Katunayake is the Air Force's largest base, with two flying squadrons. Its high-security zone overlooks the runway shared with the international airport. The base and the airport were attacked in July 2001.

milops.label: Army Headquarters housed in the Defence Headquarters Complex at Akuregoda
milops.text: The Army Headquarters is housed in the Defence Headquarters Complex at Akuregoda, Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte. The complex houses the armed forces' headquarters and the Ministry of Defence as they move there from Colombo.
milops.source: Wikipedia (Sri Lanka Army; Defence Headquarters Complex, 2026)

milops.label: Army divisions: Jaffna's headquarters at Palaly commands 51, 52 and 55 Divisions; 11 Division defends Colombo
milops.text: Except for 11 Division at Panagoda, which defends the capital, Army divisions and brigades are deployed in the Northern and Eastern provinces under regional Security Forces Headquarters. The Jaffna headquarters, at Palaly, commands 51, 52 and 55 Divisions, and 55 Division is based at Elephant Pass.
milops.source: Wikipedia (Sri Lanka Army; Security Forces Headquarters Jaffna, 2026)

milops.label: Security Forces Headquarters East at Trincomalee, with 22 Division
milops.text: The Army's Security Forces Headquarters East and 22 Division are in Trincomalee, alongside the Eastern Naval Command and the Air Force's Eastern Zonal Command.

arms.label: No nuclear power plant: five candidate sites identified for a first plant (IAEA review, July 2025)
arms.text: Sri Lanka has identified five candidate sites for a first nuclear power plant, drafted a nuclear law and set up a procurement structure, according to an IAEA follow-up review mission (14-18 July 2025). The sites are not published here.
arms.source: IAEA press release (Jul 2025); NewsFirst (Jul 2025); Nuclear Engineering International

arms.label: The long-term electricity plan keeps nuclear as an option: a 600 MWe unit after 2040 is one scenario
arms.text: The Ceylon Electricity Board's long-term plan includes nuclear power as an option. One scenario has a 600 MWe unit starting after 2040, and the plan notes that a single unit above 600 MWe would be hard for the grid to absorb. Small reactors could suit the country once they are proven.
arms.source: World Nuclear Association (Jan 2026); Nuclear Engineering International (2025)

arms.label: No radioactive-waste repository: waste management still to be developed (IAEA, 2025)
arms.text: The IAEA review said radioactive waste management needs further development. The energy minister has said that disposal and emergency procedures are being prepared. This dashboard plots no nuclear storage site for Sri Lanka.

space.label: No space-launch facility and no missile base are listed in Sri Lanka in the sources reviewed
space.text: The sources reviewed for this build list no space-launch facility and no missile base in Sri Lanka, so none is plotted. The Chinese tracking ship that berthed at Hambantota in 2022 is described above as a visiting vessel, not a base.
space.source: Sources reviewed for this build (public information)

cyber.label: The national CERT: a Coordination Centre at BMICH, Colombo, under the ICT Agency
cyber.text: The Sri Lanka CERT Coordination Centre, based at BMICH in Colombo, is the country's national CERT under the ICT Agency. In 2019, attacks on government and institutional websites were investigated by the CERT with the Signals Corps.
cyber.source: cert.gov.lk; Wikipedia (2019 cyberattacks on Sri Lanka)

social.label: The 2017 Hambantota sale: unions opposed it; the government used laws against industrial action
social.text: Trade unions opposed the 2017 sale of Hambantota port, and the government used laws against industrial action to stop a strike against the deal.

wellbeing.label: World Happiness Report 2026: Sri Lanka's rank not verified in this build
wellbeing.text: The annual report ranks countries for wellbeing. Sri Lanka's rank was not verified in this build; check the report directly.
wellbeing.source: World Happiness Report (annual); not verified in this build

darkweb.label: Ransomware claims for Sri Lanka are group claims, not confirmed victims
darkweb.text: The Ransomware.live feed filtered to Sri Lanka's country code lists claims made by groups on their own leak sites. Each claim is labelled unverified.

markers.name: SLAF Base Katunayake (beside Bandaranaike International Airport): largest Air Force base
markers.note: The largest air base of the Sri Lanka Air Force, with two lodger flying squadrons; its high-security zone adjoins the international airport (Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Bandaranaike Airport attack; SLAF Katunayake); airforce.lk (Oct 2026)

markers.name: SLAF Base Ratmalana (Colombo district): Air Force Museum; former main international airport
markers.note: Air Force base at the former Ratmalana international airport; the Air Force Museum is here (Wikipedia). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Ratmalana; Sri Lanka Air Force Museum)

markers.name: SLAF China Bay (Trincomalee): Air Force Academy; air-surveillance and air-defence radar squadrons
markers.note: The Air Force Academy and training base; 111 Air Surveillance Squadron and No. 6 Air Defence Radar Squadron operate here (migflug, 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: migflug (2026); Wikipedia (List of Sri Lankan air force bases)

markers.name: SLAF Base Hingurakgoda (Polonnaruwa district): air-defence radar squadron and attack helicopters

markers.source: migflug (2026); airforce.lk (Oct 2026)

markers.name: SLAF Base Palaly (Jaffna): shared with Jaffna International Airport since 2019
markers.note: Air Force base shared with Jaffna International Airport since 2019; the Army's Security Forces Headquarters Jaffna is at the Palaly Military Base (Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Security Forces Headquarters Jaffna; Sri Lanka Air Force, 2026)

markers.note: The Commander of the Air Force declared the Mattala station open on 2 October 2026 (airforce.lk, Oct 2026). The civil airport it shares was built with Chinese financing, according to public reporting that was not re-verified in this build.
markers.source: airforce.lk (Oct 2026); public reporting (not re-verified in this build)

markers.note: The Army Headquarters is housed in the Defence Headquarters Complex at Akuregoda (Wikipedia, 2026). The complex also houses the Ministry of Defence and the Navy and Air Force headquarters as they move there. Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Sri Lanka Army; Defence Headquarters Complex, 2026)

markers.name: Security Forces Headquarters Jaffna (Palaly Military Base): 51, 52 and 55 Divisions
markers.note: Most senior of the regional Security Forces Headquarters; it commands 51 Division (Jaffna), 52 Division (Jaffna Peninsula) and 55 Division (Elephant Pass) (Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Security Forces Headquarters Jaffna; List of Sri Lanka Army formations, 2026)

markers.name: Elephant Pass military base (Jaffna Peninsula): 55 Division
markers.note: A modern military base built in 1952; the army lost control of Elephant Pass in 2000 and later regained it; 55 Division is based here (Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Elephant Pass; 55 Division)

markers.name: Security Forces Headquarters East (Trincomalee): 22 Division and the Fort Frederick garrison
markers.note: The Army's eastern Security Forces Headquarters and 22 Division are in Trincomalee, alongside the Eastern Naval Command and the Air Force's Eastern Zonal Command (Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Hambantota International Port: deep-water port on a 99-year lease to China Merchants Port Holdings
markers.note: Opened in 2010. Under a 2017 debt-for-equity deal China Merchants Port Holdings holds a 99-year lease (about US$1.12bn), handed over in December 2017 (CSIS; Wikipedia). Sri Lanka said in 2017 that it would not be a military base for any country. A Chinese replenishment call by the tracking ship Yuan Wang 5 was made in August 2022, after Colombo asked for a deferral over security concerns (NBC News; ORF). Position approximate.
markers.source: CSIS (Game of Loans); Wikipedia (Hambantota International Port); Borneo Post / Reuters (2017); NBC News (2022); ORF (2024)

markers.name: Colombo Port City (CHEC): 269 hectares of reclaimed land, built from 2014
markers.note: Chinese-developed special economic zone on reclaimed land beside Colombo Port. CHEC has invested about US$1.4bn; it committed a further US$300m in January 2026 (Daily Mirror, Jul 2026). Full completion is not expected before 2041 (Global Construction Review, 2024). Position approximate.
markers.source: Gulf News (May 2025); Global Construction Review (2024); Daily Mirror (Jul 2026)

markers.name: Colombo South Container Terminal (China Merchants Port Holdings)
markers.note: Run by China Merchants Port Holdings, where throughput has grown strongly (The Asset, 2016). Position approximate.
markers.source: The Asset (2016); Wikipedia (China Merchants Port)

markers.name: Colombo port: research vessel Shi Yan 6 docked for replenishment (October 2023)
markers.note: The Chinese research vessel Shi Yan 6 docked in Colombo for replenishment in October 2023. Sri Lanka had said it would not allow joint research without permission (ThePrint, Oct 2023; ORF, Jan 2024). Position approximate.
markers.source: ThePrint (Oct 2023); ORF (Jan 2024)

markers.name: Colombo Dockyard PLC (Colombo Harbour): commercial shipyard that built the Colombo-class vessels for the Navy

markers.source: Wikipedia (List of active ships of the Sri Lanka Navy, 2026)

markers.name: Trincomalee oil tank farm (China Bay): 99 tanks; Ceylon Petroleum Corporation owns 24
markers.note: The Second World War-era tank farm has 99 tanks. As of August 2026, two CPC tanks had been renovated and tenders called for three more; an RFP for 29 tanks is ready, with a target of two years (CPC, Aug 2026). Other tanks are operated under separate arrangements (not described here). Position approximate.
markers.source: Tank Storage Magazine (Aug 2026); The Morning (2026); Sunday Times (May 2026)

markers.source: Wikipedia (Ceylon Electricity Board; Lakvijaya Power Station)
